pages.quiz:
COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #4
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES OCTOBER
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Binary Arithmetic Operations, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Binary Arithmetic Operations.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Binary Arithmetic Operations.

2. When learning Computer Network Standards and Protocols, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Computer Network Standards and Protocols.

3. When learning Data Representation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Representation.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Representation.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Data Representation.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Representation.

4. When learning Network Security, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Security.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Security.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Security.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Network Security.

5. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Internal Cooking Timer
   C. Information and Communication Technology
   D. Input Cable Tester

6. When learning Logic Circuits, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Logic Circuits.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Logic Circuits.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Logic Circuits.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Logic Circuits.

7. When learning Structured Query Language, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Structured Query Language.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Structured Query Language.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Structured Query Language.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Structured Query Language.

8. When learning Web Development Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Web Development Fundamentals.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Web Development Fundamentals.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Web Development Fundamentals.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Web Development Fundamentals.

9. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. CPU
   C. Monitor
   D. Speaker

10. When learning Relational Database Fundamentals, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Relational Database Fundamentals.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Relational Database Fundamentals.

11. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Overload every socket
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   D. Ignore burnt cables

12. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Wear safety gear and follow instructions
   D. Run with the tool

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Data Representation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Binary Arithmetic Operations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Gates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Logic Circuits and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
